questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the features of a plant cell listed in Column I with their corresponding examples in Column II.

Column IColumn II
i. Cell with cytoplasm and no nucleusp. Pollen grain
ii. Cell lacking both cytoplasm and nucleusq. Synergid
iii. Cell containing more than two nucleir. Tracheid
iv. Haploid cell produced by mitosiss. Tapetum
t. Mature sieve tube
u. Phloem companion cell
questions.explanation: Mature sieve tube elements (t) have cytoplasm but no nucleus. Tracheids (r) are dead cells lacking both cytoplasm and nucleus. Tapetum (s) is a multinucleate nutritive tissue. Pollen grain (p) is haploid and produced by mitosis from the haploid microspore. Phloem companion cells (u) have both cytoplasm and nucleus.
questions.imagePrompt: Two-column matching table with biological structures and their characteristics

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Shown below are some of the reactions that occur in the metabolic pathway leading to complete oxidation of glucose during aerobic respiration: (i) Pyruvate → Acetyl CoA; (ii) Dihydroxy acetone phosphate → Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate; (iii) Oxaloacetate → Citrate; (iv) Fumarate → Malate. Choose the correct sequence of reactions during the complete oxidation of glucose.
questions.explanation: Reaction (ii) occurs in glycolysis (conversion of DHAP to G3P). Reaction (i) is the link reaction (pyruvate dehydrogenase). Reaction (iii) begins the Krebs cycle (citrate synthase). Reaction (iv) occurs within the Krebs cycle (fumarase).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a flowering plant, seed coat colour is governed by a nuclear gene with two alleles (W dominant over w). If a plant with brown seeds (ww) is crossed as a female with pollen from a white seed (WW) plant, what will be the seed colour and the genotype of the embryo in the resultant seeds?
questions.explanation: The seed coat is maternal tissue (derived from integuments). Since the mother is ww (brown), all seeds will have brown seed coats regardless of the embryo's genotype. The embryo is formed from the fusion of ww (female) and W (male gamete), resulting in Ww genotype.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the COVID-19 pandemic, SARS-CoV-2 virus mutated multiple times giving rise to many variants. What is the genetic material of the SARS-CoV-2 virus?
questions.explanation: SARS-CoV-2 is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus (+ssRNA). Its genetic material consists of a single strand of RNA approximately 30,000 nucleotides long.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lymph is an important body fluid. Choose the INCORRECT statement about the lymph.
options: It remains as an interstitial fluid and is never put back into circulation
It is the interstitial fluid generated by the passage of liquid between the cells of the capillary
It is colourless and has similar mineral composition as of plasma
Fat digested in the intestine is absorbed through the lacteals
questions.explanation: Lymph is eventually returned to the circulatory system through the thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct that empty into large veins near the heart. Statements (b), (c), and (d) are correct descriptions of lymph formation, composition, and function in fat absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Interneurons play an important role in the execution of spinal cord-mediated reflex action. Where are these interneurons located?
questions.explanation: Interneurons (association neurons) are located entirely within the central nervous system, predominantly in the gray matter of the spinal cord and brain. They connect sensory and motor neurons in reflex arcs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Osmoreceptors are sensitive to changes in ionic concentrations and volumes of body fluids. Which among the following best describes the function of these osmoreceptors?
options: They stimulate hypothalamus to facilitate the release of the anti-diuretic hormone and increase water reabsorption
They stimulate pituitary gland to facilitate the secretion of mineralocorticoids to adjust the changes in mineral composition of the body fluid
They stimulate atrial wall to release atrial natriuretic factor to induce vasodilation and reduce blood pressure
They stimulate renin production to induce vasoconstriction and increase blood pressure
questions.explanation: Hypothalamic osmoreceptors detect increased blood osmolarity (dehydration) and stimulate the posterior pituitary to release ADH (vasopressin), which promotes water reabsorption in the collecting ducts of kidneys.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A single point mutation in gene 'X' results in breathing difficulty, hypertension as well as partial sterility. Which among the following phenomenon best explains the observed phenotypes?
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy occurs when a single gene influences multiple, seemingly unrelated phenotypic traits. Here, one gene mutation affects respiratory, cardiovascular, and reproductive systems simultaneously.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a cross between individuals of the genotypes PpQQRrSS and ppqqRrSS, what will be the expected number of progenies with the genotype ppQQRrSS in a population of 400 individuals, assuming independent assortment?
questions.explanation: For the QQ genotype to appear in progeny, both parents must contribute Q alleles. However, the second parent has genotype qq and can only contribute q alleles. Therefore, it is impossible to obtain QQ offspring from this cross (all offspring will be Qq). Expected number is 0.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms in which of the following phyla are triploblastic, acoelomate and have bilateral symmetry?
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are triploblastic (three germ layers), acoelomate (no body cavity), and bilaterally symmetrical. Mollusca and Arthropoda are coelomate (or reduced coelom), and Hemichordata is coelomate.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider the following biomes: P-Tropical Rainforest; Q-Tundra; R-Desert; S-Coastal zone. Choose the most probable descending order of Net Primary Productivity of these biomes.
questions.explanation: Net Primary Productivity is highest in tropical rainforests (P) due to high rainfall and temperature year-round. Coastal zones (S) also have high productivity. Tundra (Q) has low productivity due to cold temperatures. Deserts (R) have the lowest productivity due to water limitation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Nine percent of a population cannot taste a certain food item because of a recessive allele. Assuming the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, what will be the frequency of dominant and recessive alleles, respectively?
questions.explanation: Cannot taste (recessive phenotype) frequency q² = 0.09. Therefore q = √0.09 = 0.3. Dominant allele frequency p = 1 - q = 0.7. So frequencies are 0.7 (dominant) and 0.3 (recessive).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: As opposed to DNA replication within the cell, discontinuous synthesis of DNA does NOT occur in a polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Why?
options: Denaturation step in PCR substitutes for the replication fork and Taq polymerase extends DNA only in the 5′ to 3′ direction
The replication fork is formed and Taq polymerase extends DNA in both 3′ to 5′ and 5′ to 3′ direction
Denaturation step in PCR substitutes for the replication fork and Taq polymerase extends DNA only in the 3′ to 5′ direction
The replication fork is formed and DNA ligase activity of the Taq polymerase joins the discontinuous fragments
questions.explanation: In PCR, high temperature denatures DNA strands completely (no replication fork needed). Since both strands are separate and oriented appropriately, Taq polymerase can synthesize both new strands continuously in the 5'→3' direction without need for Okazaki fragments (discontinuous synthesis).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: [Image-based] Which of the following figures correctly represents the chemiosmotic hypothesis of ATP synthesis occurring in a mitochondrion? (Keys: IMS-Intermembrane space, IMM-Inner mitochondrial membrane, MM-Mitochondrial matrix, ETC-Electron transport chain)
questions.explanation: The chemiosmotic hypothesis involves proton pumping from the matrix to the intermembrane space by the ETC, creating a proton gradient. ATP synthase allows protons to flow back into the matrix, using this energy to phosphorylate ADP to ATP.
questions.imagePrompt: Diagram of mitochondria inner membrane showing ETC pumping H+ from matrix to intermembrane space, and ATP synthase allowing H+ back into matrix while synthesizing ATP from ADP+Pi

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Let 'X' be the perpendicular distance from the centromere of each chromosome to the equatorial plane of a human cell. Which of the following stages of the cell cycle is most likely to have the HIGHEST average value of 'X'?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes are aligned at the equatorial plate (X ≈ 0). During anaphase, chromosomes move toward opposite poles. In late anaphase, they are far from the equator (approaching the poles), resulting in the maximum average distance X.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The products of the reaction between aqueous solutions of K₄[Fe(CN)₆] and H₂O₂ are:
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide oxidizes ferrocyanide [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ to ferricyanide [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ (ferric form). In alkaline conditions (hydroxide produced), the products are potassium ferricyanide and potassium hydroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the colourless complex [M(H₂O)₆]ⁿ⁺, where M is a 3d transition metal, the correct ground state d-electron configuration of M is:
questions.explanation: A colourless complex in the 3d series typically has a d⁰ or d¹⁰ configuration (no d-d transitions possible). The configuration (t₂g)⁶(eg)⁴ corresponds to d¹⁰ (e.g., Zn²⁺), which is colourless. Other configurations have unpaired electrons and are coloured.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Choose the correct statement about the structure of C₆₀ fullerene.
options: 5-membered rings are fused with 6-membered rings ONLY
6-membered rings are fused with 5-membered rings ONLY
6-membered rings are fused with 6-membered rings ONLY
5-membered rings are fused with both 5-membered and 6-membered rings
questions.explanation: According to the isolated pentagon rule in fullerenes, no two pentagons share an edge (adjacent pentagons are destabilizing). Therefore, each 5-membered ring in C₆₀ is surrounded only by 6-membered rings. However, 6-membered rings are fused with both 5- and 6-membered rings.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
The first to fifth ionization energies (IE) of two p-block elements X and Y are given below:

ElementIE1 (eV)IE2 (eV)IE3 (eV)IE4 (eV)IE5 (eV)
X6.018.828.4120.0153.7
Y8.216.333.545.1166.7

The number of valence electrons in X and Y respectively are:
questions.explanation: For element X, there is a large jump between IE₃ and IE₄ (28.4 to 120.0 eV), indicating removal of the 4th electron requires breaking into a stable core, so X has 3 valence electrons. For Y, the jump is between IE₄ and IE₅ (45.1 to 166.7 eV), so Y has 4 valence electrons.
questions.imagePrompt: Table showing ionization energies IE1 through IE5 for elements X and Y with specific values highlighting the large jump

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Image-based] Which of the following expressions represents the hydrogen atom wave function ψ(r) shown in the figure? (r is the distance of the electron from the nucleus and a₀ is a constant; the graph shows a radial node at finite r)
questions.explanation: The graph shows a radial wavefunction with one radial node (crosses zero once) and starts positive. This corresponds to the 2s orbital. The 2s radial function is proportional to (2 - r/a₀)e^(-r/2a₀), which matches option A. Option B is 1s (no node), C is 2p (node at origin), D is more complex.
questions.imagePrompt: Graph plotting ψ(r) versus r/a₀ showing wavefunction starting at ~0.6, decreasing to zero around r/a₀=2, becoming negative, then approaching zero asymptotically from below

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Image-based] Which of the following molecules are aromatic? (Structures shown: M=Pyridine, N=Pyridinium ion, O=Pyrrole, P=Pyrrolium ion)
questions.explanation: Pyridine (M, 6π electrons), Pyridinium ion (N, 6π electrons from double bonds), and Pyrrole (O, 6π electrons including nitrogen lone pair) are all aromatic. Pyrrolium ion (P, protonated pyrrole) has only 4π electrons and loses aromaticity.
questions.imagePrompt: Four chemical structures labeled M (pyridine), N (pyridinium cation), O (pyrrole), and P (pyrrolium cation with two hydrogens on nitrogen)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Image-based] Which of the following are aryl bromides? (Structures: M=bromocyclopentadiene, N=bromobenzene, O=benzyl bromide, P=4-bromophenol)
questions.explanation: Aryl bromides have the bromine atom directly attached to an aromatic ring. N (bromobenzene) and P (4-bromophenol/p-bromophenol) are aryl bromides. O (benzyl bromide, Ph-CH₂-Br) is an alkyl bromide. M is bromocyclopentadiene (antiaromatic ring).
questions.imagePrompt: Four chemical structures labeled M (bromocyclopentadiene), N (bromobenzene), O (benzyl bromide), and P (p-bromophenol)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Benzamide is treated with Br₂ and NaOH(aq) to form product X, which is then reacted with NaNO₂ and HCl(aq) at 0-5°C to form Y. Y is immediately treated with ethanol to give Z. What is Z?
questions.explanation: Step 1: Hofmann degradation of benzamide gives aniline (X). Step 2: Diazotization gives benzenediazonium chloride (Y). Step 3: Treatment with ethanol reduces the diazonium group to H (replacement of -N₂⁺ with -H), yielding benzene (Z).
questions.imagePrompt: Four product structures labeled A (benzene), B (ethoxybenzene), C (aniline), and D (ethylbenzene)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the following reaction sequence, the major products M, N, and O respectively are: Phenol → (1. NaOH, 2. MeI) → M → (CH₃COCl, anhydrous AlCl₃) → N → (NaOCl) → O
options: Anisole, ortho-acylated product, sodium salicylate derivative
questions.explanation: Step 1: Phenol → Methylation of OH gives anisole (M). Step 2: Friedel-Crafts acylation at para position gives p-methoxyacetophenone (N). Step 3: Haloform reaction (NaOCl) cleaves the methyl ketone to carboxylic acid salt, p-methoxybenzoate (O).
questions.imagePrompt: Four rows showing three structures each representing possible products M, N, and O for the reaction sequence

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Image-based] The major product P of the following reaction is: (Styrene derivative + HBr)
questions.explanation: The reaction is electrophilic addition of HBr to the alkene without peroxide (Markovnikov conditions). The proton adds to form the more stable benzylic carbocation, and Br⁻ attaches to the benzylic carbon (adjacent to phenyl ring).
questions.imagePrompt: Starting material structure showing phenyl group attached to CH=CH-CH(CH3)2 chain, plus HBr reagent arrow to product P. Four product options shown.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
An aqueous solution contains 1.0 M of X2+ and 0.001 M of Y2+ ions at 25°C. X2+ and Y2+ ions do not interact with each other. This solution is put in an electrolytic cell and the voltage is gradually increased till a current begins to flow through the cell. The voltage is maintained at this point and a deposit is observed on the cathode. What is the composition of the material deposited on the cathode?

(Given: Atomic weight of X is 63 and Y is 200.
X2+ + 2e− → X, E° = 0.35 V,
Y2+ + 2e− → Y, E° = 0.40 V,
E° is the standard reduction potential.)
questions.explanation: Although Y has a higher standard reduction potential (0.40 V vs 0.35 V), at the given concentrations, the actual electrode potential for Y is E = 0.40 - (0.059/2)log(1/0.001) = 0.311 V, while for X it remains 0.35 V. Since X has the higher actual potential, X deposits first (only X deposits).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction involving ideal gases, A(g) + 2B(g) ⇋ 2C(g) + 3D(g), which of the following plots is qualitatively correct? (Kp and Kc are the equilibrium constants in terms of pressure and concentration respectively. T is the absolute temperature.)
questions.explanation: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn where Δn = (2+3)-(1+2) = 2. Therefore Kp/Kc = (RT)² ∝ T². The plot should be a parabola opening upward from the origin.
questions.imagePrompt: Four graph options showing Kp/Kc versus temperature T with different curve shapes: parabolic upward, flat horizontal, linear decreasing, and linear increasing

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The van der Waals equation is (P + a/V²)(V - b) = RT. What is the dimension of a/b?
questions.explanation: [a] = [PV²] = [Force/Area × Volume²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻² × L⁶] = [ML⁵T⁻²]. [b] = [Volume] = [L³]. Therefore [a/b] = [ML⁵T⁻²/L³] = [ML²T⁻²], which is the dimension of energy.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: 2 g of naphthoic acid (MW = 172 g/mol) dissolved in 20 mL of benzene shows freezing point depression of 2 K. For benzene, Kf = 5 K kg mol⁻¹ and density = 0.88 g/mL. What is the magnitude of the van't Hoff factor?
questions.explanation: Molality = (2/172) / (20×0.88/1000) = 0.6607 mol/kg. Using ΔTf = iKfm: i = 2 / (5 × 0.6607) = 0.605. The value less than 1 indicates association of the acid molecules in benzene (dimer formation).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Identify the correct order of the molecules with respect to the magnitude of their dipole moment: (Various dihalobenzenes)
questions.explanation: The dipole moment depends on bond moments and geometry. Para-disubstituted benzenes have zero or very small dipole moments (vectors cancel). Ortho-disubstituted have resultant vectors at 60°. C-Cl bond moment > C-F, so o-dichlorobenzene > o-difluorobenzene. The correct order places para isomers lowest and ortho-dichloro highest.
questions.imagePrompt: Four structures showing: p-difluorobenzene, p-dichlorobenzene, o-dichlorobenzene, and o-difluorobenzene with dipole moment comparison arrows

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A randomly chosen card from a deck of 52 cards is given to be a black card (Spade or Club). What is the probability that it is either a face card (King, Queen or Jack) or a Spade?
questions.explanation: Given black card (26 cards: 13 Spades, 13 Clubs). Face cards: 6 black face cards (3 in Spades, 3 in Clubs). Spades: 13 cards. Intersection (black face cards that are Spades): 3. P(Face ∪ Spade) = (6 + 13 - 3)/26 = 16/26 = 8/13.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let ω be a complex root of x² + x + 1 = 0. The value of the product (ω + 1/ω)(ω² + 1/ω²)...(ω¹⁰⁰ + 1/ω¹⁰⁰) is:
questions.explanation: Since ω³ = 1 and ω ≠ 1, we have 1/ω = ω². For k not divisible by 3, ωᵏ + ω⁻ᵏ = -1. For k divisible by 3, the term equals 2. From 1 to 100, there are 33 multiples of 3 and 67 others. Product = 2³³ × (-1)⁶⁷ = -2³³.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let f(x) = aₙxⁿ + ... + a₀ be a polynomial. Suppose f(0) = 0, f'(0) = 1, f''(0) = 4, and f''' = f⁽⁵⁾. Then f(5) =
questions.explanation: From conditions: a₀ = 0, a₁ = 1, 2a₂ = 4 ⇒ a₂ = 2. The derivative condition implies 6a₃ = 120a₅. Assuming minimal degree (cubic), a₃ = 0. Thus f(x) = 2x² + x. Therefore f(5) = 2(25) + 5 = 55.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let S be the set of all unit vectors in the XY-plane. Then the set S has:
questions.explanation: Unit vectors in the XY-plane have the form (cos θ, sin θ) for any angle θ ∈ [0, 2π). Since θ can take infinitely many values, there are infinitely many unit vectors.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: A lab reports global average temperature in 2020 was 14.9°C and predicts increase at 1% per year. What will be the temperature in 2035?

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let X be the set of all 2×2 matrices with real entries and R ⊂ X×X be the relation R = {(A,B) : AB = BA}. Which statement is true?
options: R is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
R is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
R is symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
questions.explanation: Reflexive: AA = AA, true. Symmetric: If AB = BA then BA = AB, true. Transitive: If AB = BA and BC = CB, AC = CA is not generally true for matrix multiplication (counterexample exists). Thus not transitive.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For natural number n, let Cₙ be the curve y = xⁿ (0 ≤ x ≤ 1). Let Aₙ denote the area between Cₙ and Cₙ₊₁. Then the largest value of Aₙ is:
questions.explanation: Aₙ = ∫₀¹ (xⁿ - xⁿ⁺¹) dx = 1/(n+1) - 1/(n+2) = 1/((n+1)(n+2)). This is maximized at smallest n, i.e., n = 1. Maximum value = 1/(2×3) = 1/6.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let f be continuous on [0,1] and F be its antiderivative. If F(0) = 1 and ∫₀¹ f(x)dx = 1, then F(1) is:
questions.explanation: By Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, ∫₀¹ f(x)dx = F(1) - F(0) = 1. Therefore F(1) = 1 + F(0) = 1 + 1 = 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let a ≠ 0 be real and f: R→R be continuous with f'(x) > 0 for all x. Consider g(x) = f(2a²x - ax²). Then g has:
options: Local maxima at x = a if a > 0
Local maxima at x = a if a < 0
Local minima at x = a if a > 0
Point of inflection at x = a
questions.explanation: The inner function h(x) = 2a²x - ax² has derivative h'(x) = 2a(a-x). Critical point at x = a. h''(x) = -2a. If a > 0, h''(a) = -2a < 0, so h has maximum at x = a. Since f is increasing, g inherits the maxima from h.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Let A be the 3×3 matrix with rows [cos θ, 0, -sin θ], [1, 1, 1], [sin θ, 0, cos θ]. For any natural number k, det(Aᵏ) is:
questions.explanation: det(A) = cos θ(cos θ) - 0 + (-sin θ)(-sin θ) = cos²θ + sin²θ = 1. Therefore det(Aᵏ) = (det A)ᵏ = 1ᵏ = 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For the vectors a = î + xĵ + 2k̂, b = î + 2ĵ + xk̂, c = 2î + ĵ + 3k̂, the values of x for which there is at least one nonzero vector perpendicular to all three are:
questions.explanation: A non-zero vector perpendicular to all three exists iff the vectors are coplanar (linearly dependent), i.e., scalar triple product [a b c] = 0. Computing determinant gives 2x(x-2) = 0, so x = 0 or 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: [Image-based] Consider the tangent lines to the circle x²+y²=1 at points P=(1,0) and Q=(1/√2, 1/√2). If R is the intersection of these tangents, then angle PRQ is:
questions.explanation: Tangent at P(1,0) is x = 1 (vertical). Tangent at Q is x/√2 + y/√2 = 1 or x + y = √2. Intersection R is at (1, √2-1). Vector RP = (0, -(√2-1)) (downward). Vector RQ = (1/√2 - 1, 1/√2 - (√2-1)) = (-(√2-1)/√2, ... ). The angle between the tangents at intersection point equals the angle subtended by chord PQ at the center, which is 45° (π/4).
questions.imagePrompt: Circle with center O, points P at (1,0) and Q at 45 degrees, tangent lines meeting at external point R, forming angle PRQ

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The function f(x) = 2x³ - 15x² + 36x - 5 is:
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 6x² - 30x + 36 = 6(x-2)(x-3). f'(x) > 0 when x < 2 or x > 3. Therefore f is increasing on (-∞, 2) and (3, ∞). The interval (0,2) is a subset of (-∞, 2), so f is increasing there.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: The value of the integral ∫₁¹⁰⁰ [x]/x dx, where [x] is the greatest integer function, is:
questions.explanation: Breaking into intervals [n, n+1): ∫ = Σₙ₌₁⁹⁹ ∫ₙⁿ⁺¹ n/x dx = Σₙ₌₁⁹⁹ n[ln(n+1) - ln(n)] = Σₙ₌₁⁹⁹ [ln((n+1)ⁿ/nⁿ)] = ln(Π (n+1)ⁿ/nⁿ) = ln(100⁹⁹/99!).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For arbitrary constants α, β, the differential equation representing the family of curves y = (αx + β)eˣ is:
questions.explanation: Differentiating: y' = αeˣ + (αx+β)eˣ = αeˣ + y. Thus αeˣ = y' - y. Differentiating again: y'' = αeˣ + y' = (y' - y) + y' = 2y' - y. Therefore y'' - 2y' + y = 0.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle experiences acceleration a⃗ = αv⃗. If distances traveled in time intervals t₂-t₁ and t₃-t₁ are S₁₂ and S₁₃, which relation is true?
questions.explanation: Solving dv/dt = αv gives v = v₀e^(αt). Distance x = (v₀/α)(e^(αt) - 1). Therefore S₁₂ = (v₀/α)(e^(αt₂) - e^(αt₁)) and similarly for S₁₃. Taking ratios yields the exponential difference formula.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A point mass m on a massless string of length R undergoes circular motion in a vertical plane. If the minimum tension in the string is 2mg, what is the maximum speed?
questions.explanation: Minimum tension occurs at the top: T_min + mg = mv_top²/R. Given T_min = 2mg, we get 3mg = mv_top²/R, so v_top² = 3gR. Using energy conservation: 0.5mv_max² = 0.5m(3gR) + 2mgR = 3.5mgR. Therefore v_max² = 7gR.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object released from rest from the inner edge of a hemispherical bowl with friction coefficient μ stops after angular displacement θ. Which expression relates μ and θ?
questions.explanation: Using work-energy theorem: mgR(1-cosθ) = work done by friction = ∫μN Rdθ. For equatorial position, N varies with angle. The result of the integration yields μ = tan(θ/2).
questions.imagePrompt: Hemispherical bowl cross-section with object starting at rim and sliding to position at angle θ from vertical where it stops

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Image-based] A block rests on a frictionless floor attached to a spring. In equilibrium, the right edge is distance d from the wall. When compressed by d/2 and released, the period is T. When compressed by 2d and released, the period is T₀. What is T₀/T?
questions.explanation: For amplitude A < d, the block executes SHM with period 2π√(m/k) = 2T₀' (full period). Since it doesn't hit the wall, time to return is full period. For A = 2d > d, the block hits the wall, reflects elastically, and the motion is periodic but with different effective period. Calculation of the fraction of SHM cycle before impact leads to T₀/T = 2/3.
questions.imagePrompt: Horizontal spring-mass system between two walls, with block at equilibrium distance d from right wall, showing compression distances d/2 and 2d

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A liquid of density ρ in a container weighs W. A cubic block of side L and density ρ<sub>b</sub> < ρ is pushed by a stick to completely submerge the block in the liquid without touching the bottom. If g is the acceleration due to the gravity and liquid displaced by the stick is negligible, what is the new weight of the container as registered by the weighing machine below?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze forces on the liquid/container system
Initially, weight = W.
When the block is submerged, it displaces a volume V = L³ of liquid.

Step 2: Calculate Buoyant Force
The liquid exerts an upward buoyant force on the block: FB = ρVg = ρL³g.

Step 3: Apply Newton's Third Law
By Newton's third law, the block exerts an equal and opposite downward force on the liquid of magnitude Freaction = ρL³g.

Step 4: Determine Total Force
The weighing machine measures the total downward force on the container. This includes the initial weight W plus the downward reaction force from the block.
New Weight = W + ρL³g.
questions.imagePrompt: Weighing scale with container of liquid, cubic block being pushed down by a stick attached to a support above, fully submerged

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A monoatomic ideal gas at pressure P and volume V is first adiabatically compressed to volume V/8, then isothermally expanded back to volume V. What is the final pressure?
questions.explanation: Adiabatic compression (γ=5/3 for monoatomic): P₂ = P₁(V₁/V₂)^γ = P(8)^(5/3) = P×32 = 32P. Isothermal expansion: P₂V₂ = P₃V₃ ⇒ 32P×(V/8) = P₃×V ⇒ 4P = P₃.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Image-based] A uniform string with point charges q and -q at ends passes over massless pulleys distance L apart. What is the dependence of fundamental frequency f on L?
questions.explanation: The charges attract with Coulomb force F ∝ 1/(distance)². The string between pulleys has length related to L, and tension T balances this force. For small sag, T ∝ 1/L². Since f = (1/2L')√(T/μ) and L' ∝ L, we get f ∝ (1/L)√(1/L²) ∝ 1/L².
questions.imagePrompt: Two pulleys separated by horizontal distance L, string passing over both with charges q and -q hanging vertically below each pulley, separated horizontally by L/2

questions.question: [Image-based] Two uniformly charged concentric thin spherical shells of radii r₁ (charge +Q) and r₂ (charge -Q, r₂ > r₁). How does the electrostatic potential vary with distance from the center?
questions.explanation: For r < r₁: V = kQ/r₁ - kQ/r₂ = constant. For r₁ < r < r₂: V = kQ/r - kQ/r₂ (decreasing as 1/r). For r > r₂: V = kQ/r - kQ/r = 0. The curve matches a constant then hyperbolic decay to zero.

questions.question: A thin lens made of material of refractive index n<sub>l</sub> forms the image at the position I of a point object held at O on the central axis of the lens, as is shown in the ray diagram below. Consider that the refractive index of the medium is n<sub>m</sub> and n<sub>l</sub> > n<sub>m</sub> for the figure given. Where does the image form when n<sub>l</sub> < n<sub>m</sub>?
options: At point B (between O and lens)
At point A (between O and original object position)
questions.explanation: When nl > nm, the lens is converging (as described). When nl < nm, the same lens shape becomes diverging. For a real object, a diverging lens forms a virtual image between the object and the lens (point B in the diagram).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: [Image-based] A conducting sphere of radius a with uniform volume charge density ρ. What is the electric flux through a spherical surface of radius 2a centered at a point on the surface of the charged sphere?
questions.explanation: The Gaussian sphere of radius 2a centered on the surface exactly encloses the original sphere (diameter 2a). The enclosed charge is the total charge Q = ρ(4/3)πa³. By Gauss's law, flux = Q/ε₀ = 4πa³ρ/(3ε₀).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Fission of Pu-239 releases 207 MeV. How much Pu is needed for 20,000 units of TNT explosion? (1 unit TNT = 4.184×10⁹ J)
questions.explanation: Total energy needed = 20,000 × 4.184×10⁹ J = 8.368×10¹³ J. Energy per fission = 207×10⁶ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ J = 3.312×10⁻¹¹ J. Number of atoms required = 8.368×10¹³ / 3.312×10⁻¹¹ ≈ 2.53×10²⁴. Moles = 2.53×10²⁴ / 6.022×10²³ ≈ 4.2 mol. Mass = 4.2 × 239 g ≈ 1000 g = 1 kg.
